answer: Retrospective Burst Clustering Audit. Identities are scored by how tightly their activity clusters in time and shared counterparties against a random-timing baseline over a rolling horizon; clusters crossing a statistical threshold get throttled. Like a marble dropped into a crowd, each honest identity scatters its timing, so faking that spread costs an attacker real per-identity work under a rising gale of detection risk. Detected clusters lose accumulated reputation and pending payouts, forcing re-registration at full cost.
